title: Trastuzumab SC · early breast cancer

agents.name: Trastuzumab
agents.explanation: Trastuzumab binds to the HER2 protein on cells and helps reduce HER2-driven growth and recruit immune activity. HER2 testing identifies the cancers for which this approach is used.
agents.watch: Keep echo appointments. Report breathing changes, swelling, allergic symptoms or a painful / spreading injection-site reaction.
risks: Diarrhoea, fatigue and rare serious lung effects

context_label: HER2-positive early breast cancer · SC component
purpose: Trastuzumab under the skin is part of treatment to reduce recurrence in HER2-positive early breast cancer. The wider plan can include chemotherapy, surgery, radiotherapy and endocrine treatment when indicated.
schedule_summary: Trastuzumab 600 mg under the skin every 21 days, without a loading dose, to complete one year total. Previous IV or combination-treatment trastuzumab counts towards that year; a route switch does not start a new year.

phases_note: Early and metastatic pathways have different aims and endpoints. The team confirms the applicable plan.
timeline_note: Treatment days show the planned schedule. Symptom bands are broad possibilities, not measured risk curves or guaranteed safe days.
safety_note: New breathlessness, chest pain, collapse, severe allergic symptoms or sudden serious illness need urgent assessment on any day.
teachback: What is the purpose of your treatment? Which heart or blood test is due next, and which team arranges and reviews it?
consent_support: Discuss expected benefit, alternatives, route, duration, cardiac monitoring, pregnancy / contraception, urgent contacts and individual treatment risks. Add any companion drug using its own regimen information.
urgent_extra: Report breathlessness, swelling, rapid weight gain, palpitations or persistent diarrhoea; tell staff immediately about a reaction during treatment.

support.title: Support for this medicine
support.text: Trastuzumab alone has minimal emetogenic risk. Routine chemotherapy antiemetics, steroids and growth factors are not added automatically. Previous reactions require a separate plan.

support.title: Blood and heart appointments
support.text: FBC, renal and liver profile every 6 weeks (around C3, C5, C7 if on time). Echo / MUGA every 12 weeks; around C5 for uninterrupted 21-day cycles.

support.title: Local treatment and endocrine therapy
support.text: Surgery and radiotherapy are coordinated by the MDT. When endocrine therapy is indicated, it has its own schedule and bone-health plan.

support.title: Pregnancy / contraception
support.text: Discuss pregnancy, fertility and contraception before treatment. Report pregnancy promptly; do not breastfeed during treatment or for 7 months afterwards. The team confirms the medicine-specific contraception duration.

questions.q: How long will I receive treatment?
questions.a: Trastuzumab 600 mg under the skin every 21 days, without a loading dose, to complete one year total. Previous IV or combination-treatment trastuzumab counts towards that year; a route switch does not start a new year.
Echo / MUGA every 12 weeks; around C5 for uninterrupted 21-day cycles. Existing HER2 exposure and delays affect cycle numbering; the team should give the actual due window.

If postoperative radiotherapy is indicated, it usually follows chemotherapy and may overlap with trastuzumab continuation under the MDT plan. The radiation team assesses heart / lung exposure. Endocrine therapy may also overlap when indicated.

questions.q: Does a tumour marker replace a scan?
questions.a: No. In metastatic disease it may add information to symptoms and imaging. It should not alone determine treatment changes. In symptom-free early disease it is not routine recurrence screening.

evidence.title: Trastuzumab formulation evidence
evidence.intro: This explains the study setting and its meaning. Ask the team how the evidence applies to you.
evidence.population: HannaH compared under-the-skin and intravenous trastuzumab with chemotherapy in early breast cancer.
evidence.interpretation: Longer follow-up found similar outcomes with the two formulations. This study helps explain the choice of route; it does not predict your own outcome.

items.title: Medicine identity
items.text: This card describes trastuzumab. Pertuzumab, taxanes, endocrine medicines and antibody–drug conjugates require their own treatment instructions.

chapters.title: Before treatment and between visits
chapters.intro: The team should arrange and review the tests.

items.title: Blood checks
items.text: FBC, renal and liver profile every 6 weeks (around C3, C5, C7 if on time)

items.title: Cardiac checks
items.text: Echo / MUGA every 12 weeks; around C5 for uninterrupted 21-day cycles. Baseline cardiac assessment includes ECG in EMA trastuzumab information. Further ECGs follow symptoms / cardiac plan; an ECG does not replace an echo.

items.title: After stopping
items.text: EMA trastuzumab information: cardiac assessment every 6 months after stopping, until 24 months; after anthracyclines in early disease, yearly to 5 years or longer if function falls.

chapters.title: The wider pathway
chapters.intro: Coordinate cancer medicines with local treatment and follow-up.

items.title: Scans and markers
items.text: Early disease: breast surveillance arranged after local treatment; routine CT / tumour markers are not recommended for asymptomatic recurrence screening.

items.title: Radiotherapy relationship
items.text: If postoperative radiotherapy is indicated, it usually follows chemotherapy and may overlap with trastuzumab continuation under the MDT plan. The radiation team assesses heart / lung exposure. Endocrine therapy may also overlap when indicated.

items.title: Bone health
items.text: If an aromatase inhibitor or ovarian suppression is planned, assess fracture risk and DEXA need. Repeat timing depends on results and bone treatment; this is not an automatic HER2-therapy scan.

chronology_notes.text: Blood tests and echoes follow clinical due windows. A postponed dose does not automatically postpone monitoring.

chronology_notes.title: Companion medicines
chronology_notes.text: If another cancer medicine is prescribed, its side effects, tests and supportive medicines need its own plan.

steps.title: Before your visit
steps.text: Confirm the dose, symptoms, required blood results and echo due window.

steps.title: Access and administration
steps.text: SC trastuzumab needs no IV line for this medicine. Another medicine may still need a cannula or port.

steps.title: Treatment and observation
steps.text: Injection over 2–5 minutes into alternate thighs. Observation is 30 minutes after the first injection and 15 minutes after subsequent injections, subject to approved local policy.

steps.title: After the visit
steps.text: Contact the unit to rearrange a missed dose. SC doses remain at least 3 weeks apart; no loading dose. This medicine does not routinely require a take-home pump.

details.title: Injection site
details.text: Alternate thighs and avoid tender, bruised, red or hardened skin. Tell the nurse about a persistent or worsening local reaction.

details.title: Visit length
details.text: Injection over 2–5 minutes into alternate thighs. Observation is 30 minutes after the first injection and 15 minutes after subsequent injections, subject to approved local policy.

details.title: Missed or delayed visit

monitoring_schedule.title: When your checks happen
monitoring_schedule.note: Cycle examples assume no delays and count from the first dose of this schedule. If switching route or continuing previous HER2 treatment, preserve the existing echo due date. Tests are scheduled by elapsed time and clinical need; the team owns booking and result review. NCCP remains 12-weekly during treatment, including maintenance; a longer interval needs an explicit individual specialist plan.
